title: Does VLA Even Know the Basics? Measuring Commonsense and World Knowledge Retention in Vision-Language-Action Models
models: VLM baselines: InternVL3.5-8B/38B, Ovis2.5-9B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B, Qwen3-8B/32B, Prismatic-7B, PaliGemma-3B
action_head: mixed: discrete action tokens (OpenVLA, SpatialVLA, Magma) and flow/diffusion action expert (pi0, SmolVLA, Xiaomi-R0, InternVLA-M1)
methods: Act2Answer behavioral protocol (answer a binary VQA item by placing a cube on one of two images)
layer-wise linear 'intent' probes for the correct answer
chance-normalized retention metric (max action-expert probe vs max backbone probe)
question: How much commonsense and world knowledge do VLAs retain from their VLMs, measured by whether they can act on it, and where in the network does answer-relevant information get lost?
key_findings: 1,720 binary items in 12 categories adapted from MLLM-CompBench, IconQA, MMBench, OK-VQA and VL-Think; 3,440 episodes with left/right swaps.
Primitive categories are retained: Color 82-91% for all VLAs; Shape varies (pi0 49%, OpenVLA 64%, SpatialVLA 83%, Xiaomi-R0 82%) (Table 2).
Richer categories are near chance for most VLAs: e.g. OpenVLA Emotion 48%, Counting 48%, Celebrity 50%; no VLA beats chance on Symmetry or Counting.

Magma (VQA co-trained) is the clear exception: Emotion 72%, Time 77%, PublicInfo 88%, Traffic 80%, Celebrity 94%, LivingWorld 77%. The authors read this as 'VQA co-training is associated with better retention' (RQ5).
VLMs answering by text exceed VLAs by roughly 20-40 points in most categories (RQ3); e.g. Prismatic-7B Emotion 82% vs OpenVLA 48%.
Further OpenVLA SFT on a small pick-and-place set lowers several categories (Color 89->82%, Shape 64->53%, State 49->44%) (Table 2, RQ6).

Probing: answer-relevant info is above chance in middle backbone layers and decays toward the final/action layers. Max probe accuracy prefix vs action: Magma 75.2/72.6 (retention 0.87), OpenVLA 68.7/64.6 (0.77), SmolVLA 63.2/57.7 (0.58), pi0 65.0/55.4 (0.36) (Table 3).
Appendix: pi0 fine-tuned with paraphrases or with a latent-distillation loss to a vision teacher improves Color/Shape but leaves Emotion/Attribute near chance.

benchmarks: LIBERO numbers quoted from original papers for comparison only
evidence.scale: N = 300 episodes per category (150 items x 2 layouts), Celebrity N = 140; released checkpoints, no task-specific fine-tuning except OpenVLA SFT/RL ablations
evidence.statistics: partial: binomial Wald chance band (Delta ~0.057 at N=300, ~0.083 for Celebrity) used to classify scores as above/at/below chance; no CIs on model-to-model differences; probe accuracies reported without variance; probe train/test protocol not reported
evidence.baselines: 9 VLMs evaluated with an action-free text prompt; random chance (0.5)

causal_validation: No. Probing is correlational; nothing is ablated or steered to show the decodable answer signal is used or blocked. The 'bottleneck between representation and action' is inferred from the probe-accuracy drop.
closed_loop: Yes for the behavioral benchmark (closed-loop simulated episodes, short horizon). Probing is on activations recorded from these episodes.
limitations_stated: The protocol reduces but does not fully isolate knowledge from perception and control.

Left/right swaps reveal strong side preferences on hard categories (e.g. InternVLA-M1 Traffic 87% vs 20%); swapped views are not fully independent, so the chance band is mildly anticonservative (Delta ~0.08 with N=150).
Lightweight fixes (paraphrase augmentation, latent distillation) are useful but limited.
critique: The 'VLM-VLA gap' compares text answers with cube placement, two different readout channels. Part of the gap may be readout difficulty, not lost knowledge (the same problem as VL-Think in 2510.25616).

The headline gap does not hold for pi0's own base: PaliGemma-3B is at ~47-53% on every category including Color (47%), while pi0 gets 86% on Color. For pi0 the VLA beats its source VLM, which undercuts the 'forgetting' framing for flow-head models.
Model comparisons (Magma vs others) are confounded by architecture, data, resolution and embodiment, so 'VQA co-training helps' is an association across ~7 checkpoints, not a controlled result.

Intent probes target the correct answer's side (left/right), which may be decodable from layout and image content without any 'knowledge'. Probe details (pooling over 'all tokens', split, regularization) are missing, so the 63-75% accuracies are hard to interpret.

The retention metric (max action-expert probe / max backbone probe) is undefined for OpenVLA-style models with no separate action expert, yet OpenVLA gets a value; how is not explained in the text read.
one_line: A benchmark that makes VLAs answer VQA questions by placing a cube shows they keep color and shape but sit near chance on richer concepts, with VQA co-trained Magma the main exception and probes suggesting the info fades toward the action layers.
